scope: Private isolated TrailBase source prototype real HTTP/SMTP-outage rehearsal; NOT stock behavior, SQL-reservation-candidate behavior, SDK verification, deployment readiness, or G1 signoff

tests.name: Private G1 source prototype preserves the pending identity and recovers through real HTTP/mail after SMTP outage
assertions: Stopping the owned SMTP/mail container caused real registration HTTP 424; no session/user was installed, and the protected native read returned explicit authorization status 401 or 403 (not merely an arbitrary request failure).
The genuine pending _user row's ID and password hash were captured privately after SMTP failure.
With mail restored, duplicate registration using a different password remained opaque and preserved exactly the original pending identity/hash.
The ordinary public verification-trigger HTTP route sent genuine mail for that same pending identity; its signed link confirmed the same row.
After confirmation, the ID/hash remained unchanged; replacement-password login was denied and original-password login succeeded.

tests.name: Private G1 prototype retains one identity across concurrent case-insensitive signups
assertions: Two independent ordinary HTTP clients concurrently registered the same randomly generated address with different case and passwords against one prototype server.
At least one public registration completed; neither client obtained a session.
After both requests, the depot contained exactly one pending identity for that address with a password hash.

cleanup: passed; owned TrailBase process, six pinned services, network, depot and context were cleaned; no unrelated Docker resources targeted
limitations: Two bounded macOS loopback prototype cases: one SMTP outage/recovery and one concurrent case-insensitive signup race on a single server. No browser, Linux, multi-server stress, outage during public resend, or four-hour throttle expiry matrix.
No existing-depot restart/upgrade or backup-restore rehearsal for the embedded migration; legacy ambiguity rollback was tested only in the separate native test fixture.
Native public resend throttle stays four hours; immediate retry after a failed public resend remains unsupported.
This isolated private prototype does not change stock/default evidence, the pinned baseline or the reservation-only SQL-candidate failure.
No deployment readiness or G1 signoff.
